title: Signing out does not end the session: the signed-out cookie still opens /api/auth/me and the citizen pages, although auth.ts says signing out raises the token version
where: src/app/api/auth/logout/route.ts:8 (no revokeSessions); src/lib/auth.ts:72 (comment says sign-out revokes)
repro: node tests/qa/pass6/probes/hunt2-sec/logout.mjs (fresh citizenB sign-in, POST /api/auth/logout, then reuse the old cookie)
evidence: login 200; me before 200; logout 200 (Max-Age=0); me after logout with old cookie 200; GET /citizen/track-complaints with old cookie 200
cause: logout only clears the cookie in this browser (by design for per-tab sign-ins) and never bumps users.token_version; a copied or stolen cookie keeps working for its full 7 days after the user signs out. stillValid's doc comment claims the opposite.

title: Any signed-in citizen can learn whether a mobile number belongs to a registered account: the mobile-OTP request answers 409 "already registered to another account" for a used number and 200 for a free one
repro: node tests/qa/pass6/probes/hunt2-sec/mobile-oracle.mjs (citizenB asks about citizenA's number, read in-script, and a random number)
evidence: citizenA's number -> 409 {"error":"This mobile number is already registered to another account."}; a random number -> 200 {"message":"OTP sent."}
cause: the duplicate check runs before anything and its answer is returned as is; no rate limit on the route other than the per-number OTP cooldown, so a list of numbers can be tested one by one (each new number gets its own cooldown).

title: Mobile "verification" never involves the mobile: the code goes to the account's e-mail, so any citizen can get any number (a neighbour's) marked Verified and block its real owner (409 for them afterwards)
repro: as citizenB POST /api/profile/mobile-otp/request {mobileNumber:<any 10-digit number>} -> 200 OTP sent; the code is mailed to citizenB's own e-mail ([mailer] log line "Verify your mobile number"); POST /verify with it marks that number Verified on citizenB's profile
evidence: server log: [mailer] SMTP is not configured; no email sent to qa.c…@example.test (Verify your mobile number) for a random number citizenB never owned
cause: the OTP is e-mailed instead of sent by SMS to the number being verified; the profile page then shows a green Verified chip (profile/page.tsx:491) for a number nobody proved they hold.

title: PUT /api/profile changes the mobile number with no OTP and no duplicate check, and keeps mobile_verified TRUE, so the Verified chip then stands on a number never checked
repro: after a verified number, PUT /api/profile with the usual fields and a different mobileNumber; GET /api/profile shows the new number with mobileVerified true
evidence: code path: the profile page changes the number only through /mobile-otp (page.tsx:182,206), but the PUT schema accepts mobileNumber (validators.ts:114) and the UPDATE never resets mobile_verified nor checks user_profiles for the same number on another account
cause: mobileNumber left in profileUpdateSchema and the UPDATE; the verified flag is not tied to the number it verified.

area: personal data in logs / honest status
title: With SMTP off, every OTP mail writes the account's e-mail address into the server log, and the mobile-OTP route still answers "OTP sent."
evidence: log: [mailer] SMTP is not configured; no email sent to qa.c…@example.test (Verify your mobile number); response 200 {"message":"OTP sent."}
cause: sendMail logs the recipient address; the route ignores sendMail's {ok:false, reason:"not_configured"} (mailer.ts says callers must not claim a mail was sent unless ok).

title: Forgot-password tells a registered e-mail from an unknown one, against its own comment: a second request answers with cooldownRemaining only for a real account, and the first takes ~20x longer
where: src/app/api/auth/forgot-password/request-otp/route.ts:35-41 (cooldownRemaining only on the exists branch; bcrypt + mail only there)
evidence: registered: 1st 200 in 245 ms, 2nd 200 {..., "cooldownRemaining":60}; unknown: 200 in 12 ms and 11 ms, never cooldownRemaining
cause: the generic message is kept but the cooldown field and the OTP hashing/sending happen only for an existing account. (POST /api/auth/register also answers 409 "An account with this email already exists.", register/route.ts:44, so the address space leaks there too.)

title: A citizen's profile photo is written under public/ with a guessable name (user-<id>-<ms>.png): on the running production server it is a 404, so the photo never shows; once the server restarts it is served to anyone with no sign-in
repro: node tests/qa/pass6/probes/hunt2-sec/photo.mjs (citizenB uploads a 1x1 PNG, then the returned path is fetched with no cookie)
evidence: upload 200 /uploads/profile/user-<user 1000000006>-<ms 1794…>.png; GET of that path: 404 text/html (Next serves only the public/ files present when it started)
cause: profile photos use the old public-folder pattern that complaint media moved away from (complaint-media.ts keeps files private and serves them through an auth-checked route). next start does not serve files added to public/ after start, and serves them with no check after a restart; the name is the sequential user id plus a millisecond timestamp. Note: citizenB's profile_photo now points at that 404 path.

title: The petition desk's password can never be rotated: any sign-in attempt with the desk's e-mail, by anyone and with any password, first resets its hash to a fixed one compiled into the source
where: src/app/api/auth/login/route.ts:41 (ensurePetitionLogin before the password check); src/lib/manu/login.ts:11,24-27 (FIXED_HASH; UPDATE users SET password_hash = FIXED_HASH when it differs)
repro: code path: change the desk account's password (profile/change-password or forgot-password), then POST /api/auth/login {email: PETITION_LOGIN_EMAIL, password: "x"} from any browser: the UPDATE puts the fixed hash back, so the old (possibly leaked) password works again. Not run live: the QA desk account (qa.manu@…) is not PETITION_LOGIN_EMAIL.
evidence: login.ts: `} else if (rows[0].password_hash !== FIXED_HASH) { await pool.query(`UPDATE users SET password_hash = ?, ... WHERE id = ?`, [FIXED_HASH, ...]) }`, called for every login request before the password is compared; no token_version bump, no audit row
cause: a fixed shared login was chosen so nobody has to hand out a password; the reset runs on unauthenticated input. A leaked desk password cannot be revoked, a reset/change is silently undone by anyone, and the bcrypt hash (cost 10) of the one password is in the repository for offline guessing.

title: Change-password checks the current password with no limit: a stolen session cookie can guess the account password ~20 times a second, around the sign-in limit (8 per 15 min) and the step-up limit (5 per 15 min)
repro: node tests/qa/pass6/probes/hunt2-sec/cp-guess.mjs (12 random wrong current passwords with one citizenB session; nothing is changed)
evidence: statuses 400,400,400,400,400,400,400,400,400,400,400,400 in 582 ms; every answer {"error":"Current password is incorrect."}, never a 429
cause: the route has no failure counter (factors.ts verifyFactor has one: confirm-fail:<user>, 5 per 15 min). For a staff account the guessed password then passes the "Confirm it's you" step-up meant to stop a stolen cookie from sending e-mail, exporting or deciding, and a hit changes the password and signs every other device out (revokeSessions), locking the owner out.

title: "Sign out other sessions" needs no confirmation: whoever holds a copied staff cookie can end the owner's sessions and keep a fresh 12-hour one for themselves
where: src/app/api/auth/security/route.ts:47-52 (signout_others: revokeSessions + new cookie, no requireConfirm)
repro: code path: POST /api/auth/security {action:"signout_others"} with any staff session cookie; every other session of the account is revoked and the caller gets a new cookie with the new token version
evidence: the route checks only getSessionFromCookies + isStaff, then revokeSessions(s.userId) and setAuthCookie(...) for the caller; no step-up (requireConfirm) as the other sensitive staff actions have
cause: signout_others is the recovery action for a stolen session, but it trusts the session it is meant to recover from; it should ask for the password or an e-mailed code first.

title: Any staff login, including the petition desk, can look up any District IQ e-mail by its reference (from, to with address, subject, incident), and each lookup recomputes up to 20,000 HMACs with no rate limit
evidence: code path: isStaff(role) is the only check; checkRef loads outbound_emails LIMIT 20000 and HMACs each row per request; a hit returns to=name <email>, subject, incident
cause: the reference check is meant to let a recipient confirm an e-mail is genuine, but it returns the e-mail's details to every staff account and has no per-user limit.

title: Filing a complaint has no rate limit: a signed-in citizen can file without end, each one a paid classifier call (when a model key is set), a dataset append and a case on a department's list; its JSON body is also read with no size cap
where: src/app/api/complaints/route.ts:47 (req.json() uncapped), 54-63 (only a one-at-a-time lock and a same-text-just-filed check), 191 (classifyComplaint per filing)
repro: code path: grep checkRateLimit src/app/api/complaints/route.ts finds nothing; vary the title per request and every POST files a new complaint
evidence: the media upload next to it has checkRateLimit(complaint-media:<user>, 20, 15 min); the filing route has none; body-cap.ts says any route that hands the body to a schema must read it capped
cause: the duplicate guard was added for double clicks, not for volume; no per-citizen or per-IP limit on filings.

title: The dev-only assistant preview ships in the production build: its 57 KB fixture of real Collector assistant answers (counts by department, office addresses, 29 incident ids) is in a public static chunk anyone can download, though the page itself is a 404
evidence: 200, 59,279 bytes; the chunk holds fixtures.json (headlines like "Incidents rose to 1,301 ...", department overdue/open counts, INC- ids). No names, e-mails or mobiles found.
cause: notFound() in the page stops the render, not the client chunk the build emits for the page's client component; dev pages are not excluded from the production build.
